newsitem.title: USA: Some N.Carolina crops stressed by hot, dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Some N.Carolina crops stressed by hot, dry weather.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the North Carolina Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ended Sunday, August 17.

GENERAL: True summer weather finally arrived in North Carolina. Most areas of the state experienced hot, dry conditions with some localized scattered showers. Areas that had adequate moisture earlier in the season welcomed the hotter weather to speed the progress of this year's late crops. Crops in areas already low in moisture are starting to show some damage of the prolonged dryness. Overall, most farmers would welcome a soaking rain at this stage of the season. Soil moisture is rated 8% very short, 41% short, 50% adequate, and 1% surplus (see table below). Statewide, 6.3 days were suitable for fieldwork. Activities for the week included: irrigating, spraying for sucker control, topping, harvesting and marketing of flue-cured tobacco; spraying for blue mold and harvesting burley tobacco; cutting silage; cutting hay; preparing for the corn harvest; scouting and spraying for insects on cotton and soybeans; harvesting truck crops, apples and peaches; maintaining pastures; tending livestock; and repairing equipment.

Statewide rainfall averaged 0.33 of an inch during August 10 - August 16, .9 of an inch below normal. Morganton reported a high of 2.52 inches of rain during the past week. Average temperature for the state was 78xF, 3xF above normal. The maximum average high temperature for the week was observed to be 95xF reported at Fayetteville. A minimum average low temperature of 57xF was reported at Jefferson.
